justice: Wide, flat sidewalk surface accommodates wheelchair users, reflecting basic spatial accessibility.
Complete absence of tactile paving (blind tracks) along the sidewalk severely reduces fairness for visually impaired users.
Disproportionate allocation of paved width to motor vehicle lanes compared to pedestrian zones highlights auto-centric inequity.
safety: Lack of physical guardrails between the high-speed motor vehicle lanes and the non-motorized lane poses severe risks to cyclists.
Absence of traffic calming measures (e.g., speed bumps, raised crossings) increases danger for elderly and adolescent pedestrians.
Regularly spaced streetlights along the roadway provide necessary illumination for nighttime safety.
livability: Total absence of buildings and 'eyes on the street' creates an isolated environment, reducing social safety and vibrancy for teenagers.
Lack of street furniture, such as benches, offers no resting places for older adults during daily activities.
No visible commercial storefronts or community facilities severely limits the street's ability to support daily life.
sustainability: Presence of a landscaped buffer with young trees and shrubs provides initial ecological value and green infrastructure.
Vast expanse of impermeable asphalt roadway increases stormwater runoff and exacerbates the urban heat island effect.
Absence of visible public transit infrastructure, such as bus stops or shelters, fails to support low-carbon travel options.
aesthetics: Clean, well-maintained asphalt and paved sidewalk surfaces present a tidy and organized visual appearance.
Monotonous straight road design and lack of architectural elements result in a sterile and uninteresting streetscape.
Green landscaping strip on the right side adds a necessary natural color element to an otherwise gray environment.
comfort: Lack of overhanging tree canopy shade exposes the sidewalk to direct sunlight, causing thermal discomfort for older adults in summer.
Absence of benches or resting facilities forces continuous walking, significantly reducing physical comfort for the elderly.
Wide, flat, and seamless paving of the sidewalk offers a physically comfortable and stable walking surface for mobility aids.
walkability: Continuous, unobstructed concrete sidewalk provides a clear physical path for pedestrians.
Extreme lack of shade trees and seating makes long-distance walking arduous and unattractive for older adults.
Absence of visible crosswalks or pedestrian intersections severely limits route connectivity and safe crossing opportunities.
bikeability: Wide paved shoulder lane provides dedicated space for cycling but lacks physical separation from fast-moving motor traffic.
Smooth asphalt surface without potholes or debris ensures a physically comfortable and stable ride for cyclists.
Absence of clear bicycle lane markings or color-coded paving reduces right-of-way clarity and safety against vehicles.
